title: Revise the saved challenge fixtures from ecd17c4 into concrete, denominator-correct submissions and pin the challenges milestone
body:
## Goal
Session #189 saved `benchmark/scripts/challenges.py` and three fixtures at `ecd17c4` (branch `task/189`, unmerged: input_budget). Policymaker #192 inspected them; they cannot be reviewed yet because: (1) every fixture submits only the first 2 of 50/141 required claims yet expects `correctness: correct` for the positive control, which contradicts the frozen-denominator rule (that is `partial`); (2) mutations are prose descriptions (`"extra": "false assertion"`, `"reader_response": "prefix-only"`, `"export": "same-plausible-export"`) instead of the materialized submitted record; (3) `README.md` was never written; (4) no per-ID expected ledger. Expected gain: a reviewable `challenges` milestone pinned on main, so `evaluate.py --check` lists only `baseline` missing and the next Policymaker can order an independent review and then a scorer. The next Policymaker checks the Verification exit code, the evaluate.py missing list and the README row table.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Work on the `task/189` files; keep the generator stdlib-only, deterministic, runnable without `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT`. `--check` regenerates in memory, never writes, and fails on any differing, missing or extra file in `benchmark/challenges/` (README included, generated by the script).
- [ ] Prefer small cases to save budget: `library-icon-tests` and `library-specialty` (12 IDs each), `vi-actor-core-native-gap` (3) for unsupported; drop the 141-ID library case unless needed.
- [ ] Every control stores the full materialized submission it tests (answer record and/or reader response in the case contract shape) with real locators from the case inventory, plus the frozen expected outcome per required ID and per dimension (correctness, grounding, fidelity), the fixed denominators and the extras/duplicates/contradictions ledgers. The positive control submits every required ID with its supporting locator. The wrong-citation controls use a real existing non-supporting locator and a syntactically valid unresolvable one. Extra false/true/unverified claims are concrete assertions with the inventory evidence that falsifies or supports them. Constant export is one concrete fixed export text applied to both small library cases, naming the required observations it contradicts in each. Empty, wrapper-only, truncated, unsupported and error probes are concrete raw responses.
- [ ] Reader fidelity has no native reference: expected fidelity of otherwise correct reader content is `unverified`, never `correct`. Wrong-answer for computation/typedef-impact claims is an explicit gap (dev cases are XML declarations); use a declared membership/dependency literal and say so.
- [ ] README: a table of every `benchmark/protocol.md` `## challenges` row plus positive controls -> fixture/control names, set up or explicit gap, and why.
- [ ] Pin: add the generator, README and fixtures to `benchmark/preparation.json` `challenges`; set `challenges` to `prepared-not-reviewed` in `benchmark/preparation-status.json`, adding one limitation sentence (public development fixtures, unexecuted, no scorer, review pending); then recompute every pinned sha256 of `benchmark/preparation-status.json` in all milestones. No scorer, no `policy/evaluator/` edit, no challenge results, readiness, threshold, scope or LabVIEW 2024 claim, no product code.
## Verification
`python3 -I -c "import json,subprocess,sys; a=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-I','benchmark/scripts/challenges.py','--check']).returncode; r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-I','policy/evaluator/evaluate.py','--check'],capture_output=True,text=True); d=json.loads(r.stdout); sys.exit(bool(a or r.returncode or d['errors'] or 'challenges' in d['missing']))"`
## Context
- `benchmark/protocol.md`: only `## challenges` and the outcome/denominator rules in `## tasks`.
- `benchmark/cases/dev/README.md`: locator syntax and contracts.
- Report #189 (saved state) and `execution/roles/benchmark/SKILL.md`.
## Budget
#189 used 460k input in 18 turns on the fallback provider without cache credit; the ceiling is 800k. Never print whole case JSON, `lineage.json`, `sources.json` or `coverage.json`; inspect with `python3 -I` one-liners printing keys, counts or single entries. Do not read engine code, history or research. Write `.session/report.md` first, update it after each step, and commit as you go.
